title: Warn them before it is too late.
subtitle: Nuh's mission begins with mercy
then: Ibn Kathir says Nuh was sent to warn his people {trap}before Allah's punishment befell them{/trap}, and to tell them that {reward}if they repented, it would be lifted.{/reward} The surah was revealed in Makkah when opposition to the Prophet ﷺ was growing strong.
now: The smoke alarm goes off at 3am and you are annoyed. But the alarm is not the fire. {idea}It is the warning that saves you from it.{/idea} A reminder that stings is often the kindest thing anyone does for you.
old: Warnings about punishment are harsh and negative.
new: A warning before the harm is a mercy. It means there is still time.
try: Thank someone today who once warned you about something, even if it stung.

title: O my people, I am a clear warner to you.
subtitle: He speaks to them as his own
then: Nuh does not open with condemnation. He says {idea}O my people.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says clear means {idea}making the matter apparent and plain{/idea}, so no one could say they did not understand.
now: When you want to correct your brother or a friend, how do you start? With "you always" or with "I care about you"? {idea}Nuh begins with belonging.{/idea} Clear does not mean cold.
old: When I correct someone, being blunt is enough.
new: The clearest message starts by showing I am on their side.
try: If you need to give advice today, start with one sentence of genuine care.

title: Worship Allah, be mindful of Him, and follow me.
subtitle: The whole message in three parts
then: Ibn Kathir explains taqwa here as {idea}leaving what He has forbidden and avoiding sin{/idea}, and obeying Nuh in what he commands and forbids. The message of every prophet is this short.
now: Self-help books promise seven steps, twelve habits, thirty days. Nuh's message fits on a sticky note. {idea}Worship Him. Watch yourself. Follow the guide.{/idea} The hard part is not understanding it.
old: Living faithfully must be complicated and hard to figure out.
new: The core is simple. Worship Him, be careful, follow the messenger.
try: Write these three words somewhere you will see today: worship, mindful, follow.

title: He will forgive you and give you more time.
subtitle: Obedience opens forgiveness and respite
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah would {reward}extend their lifespan and protect them{/reward} from punishment if they obeyed. He notes the hadith that {reward}maintaining family ties increases lifespan.{/reward} But {trap}when Allah's term comes, it cannot be delayed{/trap}, so hurry to obey.
now: You keep a list of things you will fix: the uncle you stopped calling, the prayer you dropped. {idea}Allah offers more time to those who return.{/idea} The appointment itself is not moving.
old: I will have time to sort things out later.
new: Returning now brings forgiveness and more time. Waiting gains nothing.
try: Call one relative you have drifted from, today, even for two minutes.

title: My Lord, I called them night and day.
subtitle: Nuh's report after centuries of effort
then: Ibn Kathir says Nuh complained to his Lord after being patient for {idea}nine hundred and fifty years.{/idea} His words mean: {idea}I did not stop calling them, night and day{/idea}, carrying out Your command.
now: You have been praying for your father to return to prayer for ten years. Gently reminding a friend for months. Nothing changes. {idea}Nuh's report to Allah is about his effort, not their response.{/idea}
old: If they still have not changed, my efforts were wasted.
new: What I report to Allah is that I kept going. The results are His.
try: Make dua tonight for one person you have been trying to help, by name.

title: The more I called, the more they ran.
subtitle: When effort seems to backfire
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}the more I called them to the truth, the more they fled from it and avoided it.{/trap} Even a prophet's best effort did not open hearts that refused to open.
now: Every time you send your friend an article about faith, they reply less. Every time you mention prayer, your teenager leaves the room. {idea}Their running is not proof you failed.{/idea} It might mean it is time to change your approach, as Nuh does next.
old: If they push away, I must be doing something wrong.
new: Some people run from the truth however well it is offered.
try: Think of someone who runs when you remind them. Try a different, softer way this week.

title: Fingers in their ears, heads under their cloaks.
subtitle: Refusing even to hear the offer of forgiveness
then: Nuh called them {reward}so that You may forgive them{/reward}, and they blocked their ears. Ibn Kathir compares it to Quraysh saying: {trap}do not listen to this Quran, make noise over it.{/trap} Sa'id bin Jubayr said they covered their heads so they could not hear.
now: Noise-cancelling headphones on the moment the khutbah starts. The volume turned up when someone mentions death. {trap}Sometimes we do not argue with the truth. We just make sure we cannot hear it.{/trap}
old: I am not rejecting anything. I am just not listening right now.
new: Blocking my ears to a reminder can be its own kind of refusal.
try: Listen to one short Quran recitation today with nothing else playing.

title: Then I called them openly.
subtitle: Changing the approach, not the message
then: After being shut out, Nuh did not stop. Ibn Kathir says {idea}openly among the people{/idea}. He went to the gatherings. The word then marks a new stage after a long effort.
now: You have tried talking to your sibling one-on-one about their choices. Maybe what they need is to see it at a family meal, or to hear it from someone else. {idea}Same message, different door.{/idea}
old: I tried once and it did not work, so there is no point.
new: When one way does not reach someone, I can try another.
try: Pick one person you gave up on reminding. Plan a new way to reach them.

title: Out loud in public, quietly in private.
subtitle: Every method he could find
then: Ibn Kathir says Nuh proclaimed {idea}with open speech and a raised voice{/idea}, and then spoke to them in private discussions. {idea}He tried various types of calling to be more effective.{/idea}
now: Some friends listen in a group. Some only open up on a long drive, just the two of you. {idea}Good advice finds the right room.{/idea} A quiet message often reaches further than a public one.
old: If they did not listen in public, they will not listen at all.
new: Some hearts open in public, some only in private. Try both.
try: Send one private, gentle message to someone instead of a group reminder.

title: Ask your Lord for forgiveness. He forgives again and again.
subtitle: The door that is never closed
then: Nuh told a people deep in idol worship to ask forgiveness. Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}accepts repentance no matter what the sin is, even disbelief and polytheism.{/reward} The word Ghaffar means He forgives repeatedly.
now: You relapse into the same habit for the fifth time this month. You think: how can I ask again? {reward}Ghaffar is the name for exactly that.{/reward} He does not tire of forgiving. Do not tire of asking.
old: I have asked forgiveness for this too many times already.
new: Allah forgives again and again. Asking again is the right move.
try: Say astaghfirullah 100 times today, spread across the day.

title: Forgiveness brings down the rain.
subtitle: Istighfar as the key to the sky
then: Ibn Kathir reports that Umar bin Al-Khattab went up to pray for rain and {idea}did nothing more than seek Allah's forgiveness{/idea} and recite these verses. Then he said: {reward}I have sought rain with the keys of the sky.{/reward}
now: Rent is due, the job offer has not come, the business is dry. You plan, you apply, you network. {idea}Add one more strategy: istighfar.{/idea} Nuh tied it directly to rain from the sky.
old: Repenting is for my soul, and money problems need practical fixes.
new: Seeking forgiveness is one of the keys Allah gave for provision.
try: Next time you worry about money today, say astaghfirullah ten times before anything else.

title: Wealth, children, gardens and rivers.
subtitle: What returning to Allah can bring here
then: Ibn Kathir says if they repented and obeyed, {reward}He would increase their provision{/reward}, their crops, their livestock, wealth and children, and gardens with rivers. He calls this {idea}invitation with encouragement{/idea} before the warning that follows.
now: Some people imagine that getting serious about faith means losing out: fewer deals, less fun, smaller life. Nuh's message says the opposite. {reward}Turning back to Allah can widen your life here too.{/reward}
old: Taking my faith seriously will make my life smaller.
new: Returning to Allah brings blessing in this life, not only the next.
try: Thank Allah for one blessing in your home today, out loud, with your family.

title: Why do you not give Allah His due greatness?
subtitle: Taking Allah lightly
then: After encouragement comes warning. Ibn Abbas said it means {trap}you do not magnify Allah as He deserves{/trap}, and do not fear His punishment. Ibn Kathir calls this balancing the invitation with caution.
now: You would never check your phone while your boss is talking to you. But in prayer, the mind wanders to lunch and messages. {idea}How we treat Allah sometimes shows how small we have made Him in our minds.{/idea}
old: Allah is forgiving, so I do not need to take Him too seriously.
new: Knowing His mercy should come with knowing His majesty.
try: Before your next prayer, pause and say Allahu akbar slowly, meaning it.

title: He created you in stages.
subtitle: Your own growth is a sign
then: Nuh points his people to their own bodies. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Qatadah and others said the stages are {idea}a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh.{/idea} The One who shaped them deserves their awe.
now: Look at your baby photos, your school photos, your face in the mirror today. {idea}You did not design any of those stages.{/idea} Someone carried you through each one.
old: I grew up the way everyone does, nothing special about it.
new: Every stage of my life was shaped by Allah. That deserves awe.
try: Look at an old photo of yourself today and thank Allah for bringing you this far.

title: Seven heavens, one above another.
subtitle: Nuh points his people to the sky

picture.label: What he asks them to see

then: Nuh moves from their bodies to the sky. Ibn Kathir says the heavens are {idea}one above another.{/idea} He notes that scholars hold many opinions on the details, but {idea}the point is Allah's creation{/idea}, set against the idols they worshipped.
now: You spend most of the day looking down: at a screen, a desk, a steering wheel. {idea}Nuh's first argument was simply: look up.{/idea} The sky is the oldest reminder there is.
old: The sky is just background to my busy life.
new: The heavens above me are a sign pointing to their Maker.
try: Step outside tonight and look up at the sky for one full minute.

title: The moon a light, the sun a lamp.
subtitle: Two lights, two different jobs
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}made a distinction between them in their light{/idea}. The sun marks day and night. The moon's light grows and shrinks to show {idea}the passing of months and years.{/idea} He links it to the verse about the moon's measured stages.
now: Your calendar app, your Ramadan countdown, your morning alarm. All of it rests on two lights you never set. {idea}Every timetable you live by is borrowed from His design.{/idea}
old: The sun and moon are just there. I never think about them.
new: The lights that run my calendar were placed with care by Allah.
try: Notice the moon's shape tonight and say subhanallah.

title: He grew you from the earth like a plant.
subtitle: Human beings as something grown
then: Ibn Kathir notes the word for growing here is repeated for emphasis, and {idea}its use here is most excellent.{/idea} Nuh tells his people they came from the earth the way a plant does, raised by Allah.
now: You water a plant on the windowsill and watch it lean toward the light. You did not make it grow. You only gave it what it needed. {idea}Allah grew you the same way, from the same ground.{/idea}
old: I made myself into who I am.
new: I was grown from the earth by Allah, like everything that lives.
try: Water a plant or touch soil today and remember where you came from.

title: Back into the earth, then out again.
subtitle: Death and resurrection in one line
then: Ibn Kathir says He returns you to the earth {idea}when you die{/idea}, and on the Day of Judgement {idea}He will repeat your creation just as He first made you.{/idea} Nuh's people, like Quraysh later, struggled with that second part.
now: You stand at a funeral, watching the earth go back over someone you loved. It feels final. {idea}The verse says the earth is holding them, not keeping them.{/idea}
old: When someone is buried, that is the end of them.
new: The earth that took us back will give us up again.
try: Make dua today for one person you know who has passed away.

title: He spread the earth out like a carpet.
subtitle: The ground you stand on is a gift
then: Ibn Kathir says He {idea}spread it out, levelled it, settled it, and steadied it with firm mountains.{/idea} Nuh lists this as a favour, a reason the people should worship the One who gave it, not their idols.
now: You roll out a prayer mat on your bedroom floor. Under it is a building, and under that is the ground, laid flat and steady. {reward}The first prayer mat was the earth itself.{/reward}
old: The ground under me is just there.
new: The steady earth I stand on was spread out for me as a gift.
try: In your next sujood, notice the ground under your forehead and thank Allah for it.

title: So you can travel its wide roads.
subtitle: Movement and freedom as signs
then: Ibn Kathir says He made it so you can {idea}settle in it and travel wherever you wish.{/idea} This closes Nuh's argument: heavenly and earthly favours, all from Allah. {idea}He alone should be worshipped{/idea}, with no partner.
now: A road trip with the windows down. A flight to see family. The commute you hate. {idea}Every road you travel runs across ground He spread out.{/idea} Nuh hoped those blessings would bring his people home to Allah.
old: Travel and freedom are just how life is.
new: Every road I travel is a favour, and a reason to thank Allah.
try: On your next journey, say the travel dua or simply bismillah as you set off.

title: They followed those whose wealth only added loss.
subtitle: Following the rich instead of the right
then: Ibn Kathir says they followed {trap}the children of the world, heedless of Allah's command{/trap}, who had wealth and children. Those things were {trap}gradual punishment and temporary respite, not honour or blessing.{/trap}
now: Your feed is full of people with big houses and big followings telling you how to live. It is easy to assume success means they are right. {idea}Wealth is not a sign of being on the right path.{/idea}
old: Successful people must know something I do not.
new: Money and influence can be a loss in disguise. They prove nothing.
try: Unfollow one account today that makes you measure life by money.

title: And they plotted a massive plot.
subtitle: Leaders who deceived their followers
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}tricked their followers into believing they were following the truth.{/trap} He cites the verse where the followers later say: {trap}it was your plotting night and day{/trap}, when you ordered us to disbelieve.
now: Someone you trust tells you everyone does it, it is fine, scholars are too strict. It sounds convincing because of who says it. {idea}Check where you are being led, not just who is leading.{/idea}
old: If people I respect say it is fine, I am safe following them.
new: Following someone does not shift my responsibility onto them.
try: Pick one thing you do just because others do it. Look up what the deen says.

title: Do not abandon Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr.
subtitle: How honouring good people became idol worship
then: Ibn Abbas said these were named after {idea}righteous men of Nuh's people.{/idea} After they died, Shaytan inspired people to erect statues of them. {trap}They were not worshipped until the builders died and the knowledge was lost.{/trap}
now: A habit that began as a reminder becomes the thing itself. A tradition loses its reason and becomes a rule. {idea}Knowledge is what keeps good things from turning into wrong ones.{/idea}
old: Small additions to worship are harmless if the intention is good.
new: When knowledge fades, good intentions can slide into serious error.
try: Learn the reason behind one practice you do today, from a reliable source.

title: They led many astray.
subtitle: The damage outlived the people who did it
then: Ibn Kathir says these idols {trap}misled a large number of people{/trap}, continuing through many generations. Ibrahim later prayed to be kept from them. Nuh, after his long struggle, asked Allah to give the stubborn wrongdoers nothing but more error.
now: The habit your kids copy. The way you speak about others in front of younger cousins. {idea}What you start can outlive you, for good or bad.{/idea}
old: What I do only affects me.
new: My example travels further than I think, long after I am gone.
try: Do one good thing today in front of a younger person, so they can copy it.

title: Because of their sins they were drowned.
subtitle: No helper besides Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says they drowned for their many sins and {trap}persistence in disbelief{/trap}, and found {trap}no helper to rescue them{/trap}. He cites Nuh's son, who said a mountain would save him, and the reply: {reward}no protector today except for the one Allah has mercy on.{/reward}
now: You have backup plans for everything: insurance, savings, a fallback job. Those are wise. {idea}But no plan is a mountain high enough on its own.{/idea} Real safety is His mercy.
old: With enough planning, I can protect myself from anything.
new: Nothing shelters me from Allah's decree except His mercy.
try: Add one dua to your morning today asking Allah for protection and mercy.

title: After 950 years, Nuh asked Allah to end it.
subtitle: A prayer made after centuries of patience
then: Ibn Kathir says Dayyar means {idea}a single one{/idea}, emphasising the request. The introduction notes this was not impatience: after centuries, Nuh saw no hope left, and {idea}his view matched Allah's own decision.{/idea} Even his own son was among the drowned.
now: You are tempted to write someone off after one bad year. Nuh waited nine and a half centuries, and only then, as a prophet, made this dua. {idea}Your job is to keep hoping for people.{/idea}
old: Some people are simply beyond hope.
new: Only Allah knows who is beyond hope. I keep praying for people.
try: Make dua for guidance for someone you have quietly written off.

title: If they remain, they will mislead Your servants.
subtitle: Nuh's reason came from long experience
then: Ibn Kathir says Nuh feared they would {trap}lead astray those Allah would create after them{/trap}. He said this {idea}due to what he knew about them{/idea} from living among them for nine hundred and fifty years. It was concern for future believers.
now: Think about what your home teaches: the jokes, the shows, the way prayer is treated. {idea}A household shapes the next generation more than any lecture.{/idea} The question is what yours is passing on.
old: What happens in my home is my private business.
new: My home passes something on to the next generation. I choose what.
try: Bring one small good habit into your home today, like saying bismillah aloud at meals.

title: Forgive me, my parents, and every believer.
subtitle: A dua that reaches every believer
then: Nuh's final words begin with forgiveness for himself, his parents, believers who entered his home, and {reward}all believing men and women{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says this includes the living and the dead, and {idea}it is recommended to pray like this{/idea}, following Nuh.
now: Your dua list is usually about your job, your exam, your health. Nuh, after 950 hard years, still remembered his parents and every believer. {reward}That includes you, thousands of years later.{/reward}
old: My duas are mainly about my own needs.
new: A good dua widens out to my parents, my home, and every believer.
try: Tonight, recite this dua of Nuh once, for yourself, your parents and all believers.
